title: Widlar current source
description: A Widlar source generates a small, well-defined output current from a larger reference without a large resistor. The reference device is the library's NMOS bias reference, diode-connected at $I_{in}$ delivered by an ideal source; the output device shares the gate but has a source resistor $R_s$, so its gate-source voltage is lower than the reference's by exactly the IR drop it develops: $V_{GS,ref} - V_{GS,out} = I_{out}*R_s$. That single equation sets the output current, and it is the one unknown this sheet solves: you pick the resistor $R_s$ and the width ratio, and the engine searches $I_{out}$ between its min and max for the current at which the output device, sized at that current, sits exactly $I_{out}*R_s$ below the reference's gate-source voltage. It is one named unknown searched in a stated range against the lookup tables, not a nodal solve. The fixed-point check reports the identity that search makes hold, and fails where the search does not settle. Because the output runs at a lower current density than the reference, its $V_{GS}$ sits below the reference's, so the difference is positive only when $I_{out} < I_{in}$. The output device's source sits $I_{out}*R_s$ above ground, declared as its $V_{SB}$. Both gates sit on the reference's diode node, so no gate is a port; the output node is held at $V_{out}$, the level of the node the source drives, and the supply the reference's ideal source draws from is a port.

params.name: I_in
params.note: reference current into the diode device

params.name: I_out
params.note: the output current: the current at which the gate-source step from the reference to the output device equals the drop that current develops across R_s. Solved, not set: the engine searches for it between min and max, so the stored value is never read. A positive step needs it below I_in

params.name: R_s
params.note: output-device source resistor; sets the gate-source difference I_out*R_s

params.name: M_ratio
params.note: output/reference width ratio (a unit-device multiple); usually 1

params.name: V_out
params.note: DC level of the node the source drives

equations.name: delta_vgs
equations.note: the actual gate-source step from the reference to the output device

equations.name: vgs_drop
equations.note: the gate-source step the resistor develops at the output current

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output resistance boosted by the local series feedback of the source resistor, with the resistor's own series contribution added back. Both source-referred generators drive current through R_s, so gmb belongs inside the factor — the same form the degenerated mirror uses. This is the number a stage loading the source sees

equations.name: V_out_min
equations.note: the output compliance floor: the output device's saturation voltage on top of the source-resistor drop. The output device's saturation region holds the output above it

checks.note: the output operating point must stay within the data's weak-inversion ceiling
the defining Widlar equation V_GS_ref - V_GS_out = I_out*R_s. The search on I_out makes it hold, so this check is the identity that search solves: it fails only where the search did not settle
a Widlar source produces a fraction of the reference current; a positive gate-source step needs I_out < I_in
